answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded reputation: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and every completed job adds to a public, onyx-hard record that cannot be forged or transferred. A newcomer starts at the wharf with no history, so it can only take small, escrowed tasks until peers attest its work; a single operator spinning up many quill-signed identities must fund each one separately, and misbehavior slashes the deposit and burns the reputation, making fake identities expensive and unprofitable.
